output.summary: Approved the G1016 design (attempt 4): as attempt 3, plus the capability rule now gives routine only when record_stale == ["inputs.base"] and the node has no live corrections, so a reopened or reclaimed correction run keeps its own capability after base moves (a deliberate, stated behaviour change for the no-lease case). Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1.

responses.review_tests:2:2: fixed: §2 now states the rule `routine` only when record_stale == ["inputs.base"] and kind_state has no live corrections (the frontier already attaches corrections to ready, reclaimable and crash-loop states, frontier.py:213-254). Decided the no-lease case: a plain start of a reopened node whose base moved (ready/stale, ["inputs.base"], corrections present) keeps its own capability instead of today's routine, recorded as a deliberate behaviour change. The reclaim case is the same. The verification bullet now uses test_design (which has inputs.base) for both plain start and reclaim; the no-corrections control still expects routine. Interfaces table updated.

output.summary: Design attempt 4: §2's routine downgrade now requires record_stale == ["inputs.base"] AND no live corrections, on both the reclaim and the plain-start path; a plain start of a reopened node after base moved now keeps its own capability (deliberate change). Verification moved to test_design. Everything else unchanged from attempt 3.

Resubmit of the attempt-3 implementation (f9117d0: one shared capability rule for next and cards) after the frozen tests gained the next assertions (521d78b) requested by the implementer's finding. No code change needed. Verified at HEAD: card_ux, lifecycle, schemas, journeys and docs, 100 tests OK.

Approved. Attempt 4 adds only the corrections condition to the routine downgrade, with reclaim and no-lease decisions, a table row and test_design verification. Every state card.build receives carries corrections (frontier.py:209-254; forced running is re-evaluated by lease_state; dispute and human-blocked states are refused before build). The no-lease change from routine to the node's own capability is stated and correct. review_design:2:1 is still resolved.

findings.text: render.capability (render.py:82-88) still returns `routine` for `stale_because == ["inputs.base"]` regardless of corrections, so `next` advertises routine for a reopened correction run whose base moved, while the card says the node's own tier (probe: test_plain_start_of_reopened_node_after_base_moved_keeps_its_capability setup + `next --goal`: action capability routine, corrections 1; card run.capability reasoning). Consequence: next and card contradict each other on the very case design attempt 4 deliberately changed, and anything routing from next's capability hands correction work to a routine model. Fix: apply the same rule in render.capability (at least `and not state.get("corrections")`), ideally via one shared predicate used by card.build and render.capability, and add a `next` capability assertion beside the capability tests.

output.summary: f9117d0 shares one capability rule (render.run_capability) between next actions and task cards. The card's behavior is unchanged, and next no longer downgrades correction runs to routine. 521d78b checks next's capability in all three capability scenarios. Since 8da55ca only card.py, render.py and the card UX test changed. run_tests passed. The reclaim mismatch, where next over-provisions, is a known follow-up.

Approved. 521d78b's plain-start next assertion fails on the pre-fix render/card (('routine',1)) and passes after; all 30 card_ux tests pass. The reclaim-case next assertion cannot tell old from new code because a reclaimable frontier state has no stale_because/record_stale, so next always shows the node's own tier there. That is not material: the reclaim card assertion already covers the design promise, and the next assertion still guards against regressions. Non-blocking implementation note: for a pure-rebase reclaim, next shows reasoning while the card gives routine (this already happened before the fix, errs safe, and the design promises nothing about it).

spec:
Dogfooding Release 1 (2026-11-01) found several places where workers were misled or under-informed by cards and lease verbs. Fix them together:
1. `abandon` prints the exact restart command (`start G X --as <LABEL> --reclaim`). Plain `start` after an abandon is refused without `--reclaim`, which misled the root agent.
2. A card issued by a reclaim (or any start) whose node's inputs changed since the previous attempt carries `stale_because` and a pointer to what changed (for example the old and new spec blobs or a diff command). Today it says `reason: reclaim` only.
3. A `submit` refused because findings arrived while the worker ran (responses are checked against findings live at submit time) lists those findings with their text and targets, so the worker can answer them without re-reading state.
4. The card's `output_schema` states that a finding reopens its target node. Coordinate with G1000, which adds materiality and non-blocking notes; this item only makes the consequence explicit in whatever form G1000 lands.
5. The task card's top-level `renew` prose and `commands.renew` are merged or clearly labelled, so the runnable command is obvious.
6. CLI_USAGE documents that ZZZOPS_TRACE records network git and gh calls only.
Acceptance: engine tests for 1-3 (abandon output; reclaim card after a spec edit has stale_because; submit refusal lists the new findings); card snapshot tests for 4-5; docs for 6. No extra fetches. Coordinate with G1014, which adds live-lease entries and renew's inputs_changed (reuse its helper for item 2).
title: Make task cards and lease verbs explain restarts, staleness and findings
